BW_CHIP_SCORE.result: BW is complete across 396 comparable DEV cells: 264 published Q1/ICC cells plus 132 GLOBAL_P64 cells from job 166479. On common mu_D, fixed G_ref, the fixed local512/P64anchor64 adapter and each-weight CAL11 Q1 calibration, source-equal Chip risk is 0.011515711132288248 (W_O) and 0.011497516244445822 (W_D), 22.7264% and 22.8347% below Q1. Chip improves all 11 source means under each weight and 116/132 source-site-weight pairs. theta_Chip=-1.5525868901335646e-5, 0.4584% of the original absolute method gap; high=-3.24111379e-5 and low=+1.35940007e-6. This small tested mean weight contrast is conditional on these states/calibrations/configuration; it does not prove general weight independence. Analytic HIT-path MACs are Chip 52428800, Q1 26214400, ICC 19398656 per token; cache bytes per token are Chip/ICC 37888 and Q1 10240. Full anchor+hit main-MAC ratios versus dense are Q1 0.685185185, Global-P64 0.685690427 (N=31668, including proxy), and ICC two-residual 0.637037037. Q1 pays an extra d-squared anchor projection, so the full-cycle Global/Q1 main budgets are nearly equal despite the 2x hit ratio. Native latency and video-quality superiority do not follow from local mean risk. Chip is a fixed selector and has no separate CAL parameter fit.
